ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory pre-incorporation screening of all shareholders, directors, and UBOs against OFAC SDN list, UN Security Council Consolidated List, EU Consolidated Financial Sanctions List, and Panama's UAF (Unidad de Análisis Financiero) domestic financial intelligence list. PEPs require enhanced due diligence, senior management approval, and continuous transaction monitoring under Law 23 of 2015; risk tier for jewelry/watches e-commerce is Medium_Risk_Enhanced.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Registro Público de Panamá – Dirección General de Registro de Personas Jurídicas (online portal: www.registro-publico.gob.pa)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Company names must be written in Latin script; Spanish is the official language for registration. Non-Spanish names must be accompanied by a Spanish transliteration or descriptive translation for official filing; permitted corporate suffixes include S.A., Inc., Corp., Ltd., and equivalents.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Upon rejection, the applicant may file an administrative reconsideration (recurso de reconsideración) with the Director General of the Public Registry within 5 business days, attaching arguments of non-conflict and supporting corporate documents. If denied at second instance, a fresh name clearance request can be submitted after 1 business day using a modified name. After exhaustion of administrative remedies, a judicial appeal may be lodged before the Third Chamber of the Supreme Court of Panama within two months.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Permissible for non-licensed e-commerce operations. A physical office in Panama is not mandatory; the registered agent's office is sufficient for incorporation. Virtual remote management is recognized, provided the registered agent and resident agent obligations are maintained. If the company later generates Panama-source revenue, a tax registration address and possibly a local place of business may be required.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Low to moderate – approximately 10% probability of an unannounced physical inspection during the first 12 months for a non-licensed online retailer; risk increases to 25% if the company opens a Panama bank account or engages in significant local payment collections.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Ley General de Sociedades Anónimas (Law No. 32 of 1927), as amended by Laws 3 of 2016, 52 of 2016, and 138 of 2020; supplemented by the Código de Comercio of Panama, Executive Decree No. 919 of 2018 and the Regulations of the Registro Público de Panamá (Title VI, Mercantile Section).
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Registro Público de Panamá – Departamento de Registro de Personas Jurídicas y de la Sección Mercantil (Panama Public Registry, Mercantile Division)
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Escritura Pública de Constitución de Sociedad Anónima (Public Deed of Incorporation / Articles of Incorporation, approved by notarial protocol and inscribed in the Mercantile Register)
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No minimum paid-up capital is mandated by Panamanian law for a Sociedad Anónima; articles commonly fix an authorized capital of US$10,000.00 divided into shares of US$1.00 par value, but the entire amount may remain unpaid. No escrow, deposit or capital-subscription bank account requirement applies at incorporation.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED, that the ratification and adoption of the Sociedad Anónima's Escritura Pública, as duly inscribed in the Mercantile Section of the Registro Público de Panamá under Folio No. [___], be and is hereby confirmed. RESOLVED, that the subscription by the founding shareholder of 10,000 common shares of US$1.00 par value, fully credited against cash, intellectual property and services, be accepted. RESOLVED, that the Registered Office at [street address], Panama City, Republic of Panama, be adopted as the statutory seat. RESOLVED, that the appointment of the President, Vice-President, Secretary and Treasurer be confirmed, with any two officers jointly authorized to execute banking, tax, commercial and licensing instruments. RESOLVED, that the issuance of share certificates, adoption of the corporate seal, and opening of corporate bank accounts be unanimously approved.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Corporate Name Availability Search and Reservation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registro Público de Panamá – Departamento de Registro de Personas Jurídicas (online via SIRDI platform or in-person at the Public Registry window)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit a written application or online query stating two proposed corporate names in the format 'X Jewelry, S.A.' accompanied by a copy of the applicant's passport and payment of the search fee. The Registry issues a 'Certificado de Búsqueda de Nombre' confirming availability. The name is not formally reserved unless a formal reservation request is filed and the applicant is scheduled for incorporation filing; the certificate is valid for a limited administrative period.
required_dossiers: Application letter naming two proposed corporate names
Passport copy of the incorporating shareholder or authorized attorney
Name search fee receipt (US$25.00 approximate)
Power of attorney if acting through a resident agent (notarized and apostilled when foreign)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the chosen name is flagged as similar or reserved, within 5 business days submit a written reconsideration request arguing distinctiveness, or amend the application with alternative names; no additional fee is charged for the second search within the same application.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Drafting, Execution and Notarization of the Escritura Pública de Constitución
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Notaría Pública de circuito de la Ciudad de Panamá (Notary Public of the Panama City circuit)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Engage a Panamanian licensed attorney to draft the Articles of Incorporation (Pacto Social) containing corporate name, purpose (including online retail of jewelry, watches and fashion accessories), authorized capital, share classes, directors, resident agent appointment, and duration. The incorporating shareholder(s) and the resident agent must appear before the notary in person or by special power of attorney to execute the public deed. The notary authenticates the instrument and returns the protocol copy for registry submission. All non-Spanish documents require certified Spanish translation.
required_dossiers: Draft Escritura Pública de Constitución prepared by a Panamanian attorney
Certificate of name search from the Registro Público
Passport copies of each subscribing shareholder and director
Power of attorney for resident agent, if applicable (notarized and apostilled or consularized)
Evidence of registered office address (lease or title deed)
Notarial fee payment receipt
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the notary identifies omissions or inconsistencies, the drafting attorney will issue an addendum (Acta de Corrección) to be re-notarized before the same or a different notary; re-execution is completed within 2 business days without re-running the name search if the corporate name is unchanged.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Inscription of the Sociedad Anónima in the Mercantile Register
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registro Público de Panamá – Sección Mercantil (Public Registry, Mercantile Section)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Formally file the notarized public deed at the Mercantile Section counter of the Registro Público, paying the registry fee assessed on the basis of the company's authorized capital. The Registry examines the deed for statutory compliance, assigns a corporate folio (Persona Jurídica), issues the Certificate of Registry, and publishes the constitutional edict. The legal personality of the Sociedad Anónima is effective from the date of filing; third-party enforceability is perfected upon registration.
required_dossiers: Primera copia (original certified copy) of the notarized public deed
Copy of the name search certificate
Registration fee receipt issued by the Registro Público treasury window
Filing form or cover sheet of the Mercantile Section
Power of attorney of the presenting attorney, if applicable
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Registry issues an inadmissibility or correction order (Prevención), the presenting attorney must cure the stated defect within the order's statutory deadline (generally 15 business days) by filing a corrective addendum; failure to cure may require a new filing. A reconsideration petition (Recurso de Reconsideración) is available within 3 business days against a final rejection.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Publication of the Constitutional Edict in a Local Newspaper
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Notaría o Registro Público de Panamá – Edicts Section, through authorized national gazette newspapers
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Within the statutorily prescribed period following inscription, the appointed attorney prepares and publishes the edicto de incorporación (corporate formation notice) in a Panama City daily newspaper established in the Official Gazette system. The publisher issues a certificate of publication (certificación de edicto) that must be filed with the Registro Público to complete the formation record.
required_dossiers: Certified copy of the registered Escritura Pública
Edict text prepared and signed by the corporate attorney
Publication fee receipt from the newspaper
Registry folio number of the incorporated entity
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If publication is delayed or rejected by the newspaper due to content defects, the attorney corrects the text and republishes within 2 business days; the Registry accepts the later certificate without penalty provided the edict is filed before the legal deadline.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Tax Registration (RUC) and Fiscal Domicile Registration
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Dirección General de Ingresos (DGI) – Ministerio de Economía y Finanzas, Panama (online through Sede Electrónica / 'E-Tax' portal)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File the application for inscription in the Registro Único de Contribuyentes (RUC) using the corporation's newly issued Registry folio and fiscal address. Attach the certified incorporation deed, resident agent details, and authorized capital statement. The DGI issues the RUC certificate and assigns the company an import/export code and applicable fiscal obligations. The company must also elect its territorial taxation status and register the e-commerce operational address.
required_dossiers: Certificate of incorporation issued by the Registro Público de Panamá
Copy of the published edict certificate
Administrator/representative passport and RUC card, if already held
Proof of fiscal address (utility bill or lease agreement)
Form 601 application for RUC inscription
Appointment of fiscal representative if registered address is only a resident agent's office
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the DGI queries supporting documents, within 5 business days submit the corrected form or a written clarification with certified translations; a formal appeal under the Código de Procedimiento Tributario is available against a rejection of the RUC application.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Municipal Operating Notice, Business License and Post-Registration Corporate Opening
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Municipio de Panamá – Dirección de Rentas Municipales and the local fire brigade inspection office (Benemérito Cuerpo de Bomberos de Panamá)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After RUC issuance, file the Aviso de Operación (business operation notice) with the Municipality of Panama, declaring the online retail activity of jewelry, watches and fashion accessories, the commercial premises (warehouse or business office), and the payroll if any. Pay the proportionally calculated municipal patent fee and submit the application for the fire-safety inspection of the premises. Once inspection is passed, the municipality issues the Patente Municipal (Commercial Patent/License) and the company may lawfully commence operations.
required_dossiers: RUC certificate of the corporation
Aviso de Operación form sheet (Formulario municipal)
Copy of lease or title deed of the commercial premises
Fire-safety inspection request and fee receipt
Copy of the prior year structural compliance certificate, if required for the premises
Corporate resolution naming the municipal legal representative
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the municipality rejects the operating license due to zoning, fire-safety or documentation deficiencies, the company has the right to cure by submitting revised plans, a new fire-safety certificate, or an addendum to the lease; an administrative appeal may be lodged before the Municipal Council within 5 business days of the adverse resolution.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Ministerio de Comercio e Industrias (MICI) together with the Municipality of the district where the commercial warehouse or office is located; no formal industrial manufacturing license is required for e-commerce-only retail of jewelry and watches.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Patente Municipal / Aviso de Operación (Municipal Operating Patent and Business Operation Notice) for the commercial activity 'Retail sale via Internet of jewelry, watches and fashion accessories'.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Ministerio de Ambiente (MiAMBIENTE) – Dirección de Evaluación de Impacto Ambiental, Republic of Panama
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt / Category I (Registration No. 1: low-impact commercial activity). Online retail, warehousing and distribution of jewelry, watches and fashion goods with no heavy manufacturing process is classified as a low-impact activity; a full Environmental Impact Assessment (Estudio de Impacto Ambiental) is not required unless the operation includes electroplating, metal casting, polishing waste discharges or hazardous chemical usage.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: If only storage, picking, packing and courier dispatch are performed, no industrial wastewater discharge or VOC emission threshold applies; the operator must comply with Panamanian solid waste regulations (Law 1 of 2022 and municipal waste contracts) and, should any jewelry polishing or watch repair activity with water use or dust generation be added, MiAMBIENTE requires compliance with Executive Decree No. 5 of 2021 water quality limits and National Air Quality Regulation (Decree No. 247 of 2019).

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire Safety Certificate issued by the Benemérito Cuerpo de Bomberos de Panamá (Fire Department of Panama) after on-site inspection of emergency exits, extinguishers, electrical panels and storage racking loads; structural load inspection certificate for any racked warehouse over 500 kg/m²; workplace health and safety clearance from the Ministerio de Trabajo y Desarrollo Laboral (MITRADEL) pursuant to Law 42 of 2016, including the occupational risk assessment and OSHA-equivalent safety protocols for staff handling parcel shipments.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Dirección General de Ingresos (DGI) of the Ministerio de Economía y Finanzas (MEF); digital taxpayer portal: SICE (Sistema Informático de Recaudación de Ingresos) at sice.dgi.gob.pa; official electronic-invoicing application: 'FACTURA' (Sistema de Facturación Electrónica de Panamá); customs counterpart: Dirección General de Aduanas (DGA).
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: Step 1: File the municipal Aviso de Operación with the relevant Alcaldía and record the Escritura Pública (public deed of incorporation) in the Registro Público. Step 2: The resident agent (abogado) submits the RUC (Registro Único de Contribuyente) application through SICE, attaching the certified incorporation deed, by-laws, tax domicile address, notarized identification of directors, legal representative, and ultimate beneficial owner (AML/KYC documentation), a Panamanian bank reference, and the AIG-issued digital signature certificate (Firma Electrónica). Step 3: DGI validates the application and issues the permanent RUC number, activating the ITBMS obligations and electronic-invoicing profile for the e-commerce activity code. Step 4: Maintain the 'Paz y Salvo' (tax-clearance) status, renew the RUC records annually or upon any change in activity, address, or legal representation, and retain certified corporate books required for tax audits.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: No Panamanian analogue to the US check-the-box election exists; the Sociedad Anónima is a per-se corporation subject to entity-level taxation with no pass-through of income or losses. Available statutory elections: (i) simplified Small-Taxpayer Regime for entities with annual gross income up to USD 150,000, allowing a final 2% gross-receipts ISR and simplified monthly ITBMS compliance in lieu of the ordinary net-income rules; (ii) annual election between the regular graduated ISR (15% on the first USD 50,000 of net taxable income, 25% on the excess) and the alternative minimum tax (4.7% of net assessable income, subject to a 2%-of-gross-income floor); (iii) election for tax-neutral corporate reorganizations, subject to advance DGI authorization; (iv) application of treaty benefits under the ratified double-taxation network (Barbados, France, Mexico, Portugal, Qatar, UAE) only upon satisfaction of beneficial-ownership and substance conditions. Hybrid-mismatch and check-the-box elections are foreign-law constructs with no domestic statutory analogue.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: The Republic of Panama operates without a central bank; monetary affairs are handled indirectly through full dollarization. Banking supervision and regulation are vested in the Superintendency of Banks of Panama (Superintendencia de Bancos de Panamá, SBP), while the state-owned Banco Nacional de Panamá functions as the government fiscal agent and as the operator of the local clearing mechanism. The Ministry of Economy and Finance (MEF) has no exchange-control mandate. There is no national monetary authority empowered to impose currency controls or to issue fiat currency.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Panama is a fully dollarized economy: the U.S. dollar is legal tender and circulates as the effective domestic currency, and the balboa is a nominal unit at a fixed 1:1 parity with no independent note issuance. Both current-account and capital-account transactions are fully convertible, with no exchange-control law, no central bank FX intervention, and no administrative restrictions on capital inflows, outflows, or profit repatriation. Dividends, branch remittances, and shareholder distributions from a Panama Sociedad Anónima may be effectuated freely through licensed banks in USD or any freely convertible currency. The only practical hurdles are compliance-driven: the bank's AML/KYC due diligence under Law 23 of 2015 and SBP regulations, the filing of currency-transaction and suspicious-transaction reports when applicable, and the need to demonstrate economic substance for any entity engaged in distribution and international business activity.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: None. Panama imposes no statutory timeline, no minimum hold period, and no mandatory conversion ratio for export proceeds. Export receipts in USD or other convertible currencies may be retained in full in any licensed bank account without an obligation to convert, repatriate, sell to the government, or declare to a central bank. For the e-commerce export of jewelry, watches, and fashion accessories, the absence of an FX surrender regime means that only standard SBP transaction-reporting thresholds (CTR/STR) and the entity's own accounting records govern the treatment of export revenues.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Operational USD checking account and optional Capital Escrow Account
Operational corporate USD account with digital banking and trade finance
Operational USD account and escrow-facilitating structure for non-resident-owned S.A.
Operational USD account optimized for e-commerce settlement and card-acquiring flows
Operational USD account (state bank; stricter onboarding for non-resident-owned e-commerce entities)
Operational USD account and Capital Escrow Account with higher appetite for cross-border merchants
Operational USD account; viable for trade-finance-linked treasury structures

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility rating: MEDIUM, CONDITIONAL. Panama law prohibits the unlicensed taking of deposits and the operation of payment services; the SBP digital banking license introduced by Law 160 of 2020 requires substantial capital and a local compliance presence, making it impractical for a single e-commerce S.A. Offshore digital EMIs (e.g., Wise, Airwallex, U.S. neobanks) cannot maintain a panamanian deposit account without an SBP-licensed intermediary and are therefore usable only as auxiliary settlement rails that aggregate or disburse funds into a fully licensed local bank account. For the PA_CORP jewelry/watch e-commerce model, Stripe and PayPal are permissible gateway processors, but their net settlements must discharge into a licensed Panama commercial bank account; any gateway balance cannot constitute an unlicensed stored-value or deposit-taking scheme. Legal constraint: the EMI/gateway should be screened for AML compliance and sanctions exposure, and the local licensed account must remain the treasury anchor for all concentration, counterparty risk, and audit-trail purposes.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Panama's statutory framework does not universally require physical attendance for corporate account opening, but SBP AML/CFT guidelines (implementing Law 23 of 2015) require banks to positively identify beneficial owners and authorized signatories, and in practice panamanian banks apply enhanced due diligence to non-resident-owned S.A. structures engaged in high-value goods e-commerce. Physical presence of the ultimate beneficial owner and at least one director is generally required for the initial onboarding interview, including notarized and apostilled corporate resolutions, passport certification, and a completed compliance questionnaire. Purely remote opening is available only at selected institutions (e.g., Towerbank, Banco General under certain inbound corridors) via video-KYC, independent director verification, and elevated compliance fees. For the PA_CORP structure, the recommended path is an in-person interview at a Panama branch or the bank's regional office, supported by a notarized and apostilled board resolution and a legalized certificate of incumbency, so as to minimize remediation cycles and account freezes.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High-value goods typology: jewelry and fine watches are treated as value-transfer vehicles; banks escalate any invoice mismatch, back-to-back shipments, or unexplained consignment flows.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Provide (i) supplier proformas and final invoices with harmonized commodity codes; (ii) airway bills/courier manifests and Panama customs export declarations (DUI) for each dispatch; (iii) gateway payout statements from Stripe and PayPal showing per-transaction net settlement; (iv) a refund/chargeback ratio below 2%; and (v) a documented wholesale-vs-retail pricing policy substantiating gross margins.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Historic Panama S.A. opacity and bearer-share legacy: banks will scrutinize shareholding continuity and any possible bearer instruments notwithstanding the post-2017 immobilization amendments to Panama's corporations law.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Deliver the registered share ledger and the share certificates in registered form; the apostilled certificate of incumbency issued by the registered agent; and a statement confirming the immobilization and non-existence of bearer instruments, evidencing a clear chain from ultimate beneficial owner to authorized signatory.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Economic substance deficiency: the S.A. is domiciled in Panama but administers e-commerce contracts abroad, prompting suspicion that the structure exists solely to avoid financial reporting or tax transparency.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Submit the annual Economic Substance declaration filed with the Dirección General de Ingresos (DGI) where the distribution and international business activity applies; evidence of a Panama-domiciled corporate address and registered agent; board minutes approving treasury signatories; and payroll, lease, or fixed-base records demonstrating adequate substance relative to the e-commerce activity.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Cross-border payment anomalies: card-not-present jewelry sales, settlement from high-risk acquirers, and volume spikes inconsistent with a newly formed S.A. may generate STR/CTR filings.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Maintain gateway-level transaction integrity proofs (settlement batch reports, payment IDs, chargeback adjudication records); implement the S.A.'s own KYC file for wholesale B2B clients; and submit a complete list of supplier bank identifiers (SWIFT/BIC) and trade documents to enable full traceability of each payment flow.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Source-of-funds opacity among foreign shareholders, refusal to produce wealth documentation, or sanctions/PEP screening mismatches.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Issue signed declarations of source of funds and source of wealth for each shareholder; provide audited or CPA-reviewed financial statements; produce prior-jurisdiction tax filings; and document that all capital injections occurred through formal banking channels using SWIFT remittances, excluding cash and cryptocurrency touchpoints.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Capital contributions to PA_CORP are routed as USD wire transfers via SWIFT MT103 from the shareholder's home bank to the panamanian beneficiary account at any licensed commercial bank. Because Panama maintains no exchange-control filings or fund-admission forms, the receiving bank relies on the remittance purpose and the underlying corporate legal file to classify the inflow as equity subscription or shareholder loan. Recommended protocols: use the registered corporate legal name exactly as recorded, include the registered agent reference, and state the memo as 'CAPITAL INJECTION - EQUITY SUBSCRIPTION' or 'SHAREHOLDER LOAN - LOAN AGREEMENT DD MON YYYY'; append the notarized and apostilled share issuance resolution, the updated share register, and, for loans, the executed loan agreement and repayment schedule. No prior SBP approval is required, but amounts above the bank's internal threshold require a source-of-funds statement. For gateway-originated inflows from Stripe and PayPal, settlement is effected through card-network clearing (Visa/Mastercard) into the gateway's U.S. clearing bank and then onward via U.S. Fedwire/ACH to the Panama bank's correspondent (typically Citibank N.A., JPMorgan Chase, or Bank of America), ultimately crediting the licensed local operational account.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Supplier payments for jewelry, watch inventory, and logistics are executed primarily in U.S. dollars through SWIFT MT103 credit transfers via the bank's New York correspondent network, ensuring settlement in same-day USD for beneficiaries in the United States, Switzerland, Hong Kong, and other sourcing markets. For significant or confirmed purchase orders of fine timepieces, a commercial letter of credit (governed by UCP 600) may be opened through the same bank to mitigate shipment risk; for routine e-commerce restocking, bank checks and the domestic Panama clearing house (Cámara de Compensación operated by Banco Nacional de Panamá) suffice for local service providers. Every outbound transfer should include the UETR (unique end-to-end transaction reference) embedded in the MT103 to enable straight-through processing and full audit traceability. The S.A. should retain proforma invoices, final invoices, Panama customs export declarations (DUI), courier waybills, and gateway payout statements to correlate each disbursement with the corresponding trade flow. Where payments are made in EUR or GBP, the bank converts at the onshore spot rate with full FX transparency; no surrender, license, or central bank approval applies.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Plain vanilla deliverable FX forward contracts (USD versus EUR, GBP, CHF, JPY, and regional currencies such as CRC and COP) traded with SBP-licensed banks as counterparties.

Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) referencing emerging-market currencies to hedge receivables mismatches; NDFs referencing the balboa/USD parity are irrelevant because the peg is fixed at 1:1 and fully dollarized.
Cross-currency swaps and cross-currency interest-rate swaps converting USD-denominated financing into EUR, GBP, CHF, or JPY obligations, executed under ISDA/CSA documentation with SBP-licensed banks.

Foreign-currency options (EUR/USD, GBP/USD) and gold-price-linked hedging structures protecting the value of fine jewelry and precious-metal inventory against commodity price to affect the merchant's working capital.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Franchise Tax (Tasa Única) — Payment and Sworn Declaration
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Dirección General de Ingresos (DGI), Ministry of Economy and Finance; coordination with the Public Registry of Panama
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Automatic late penalty of USD 300 plus interest; company loses legal standing before Panamanian judicial and administrative authorities; sustained non-payment leads to administrative strike-off from the Public Registry.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Corporate Income Tax Return (Declaración Jurada Anual de Impuesto sobre la Renta)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Dirección General de Ingresos (DGI), Ministry of Economy and Finance
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: On or before March 31 following the close of the calendar tax year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Penalty of 10% of the tax payable, 10% annual late interest, and fines up to USD 5,000 per non‑filed return; continued non‑compliance may result in tax classification as 'not active', RUC suspension, and registry strike-off.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Beneficial Owner Annual Confirmation (Declaración de Beneficiario Final)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Beneficial Ownership Registry, Dirección General de Ingresos (DGI)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 30 days after the anniversary date of incorporation, and within 30 days after any change in beneficial ownership
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Administrative fines up to USD 10,000 for late filing, omission, or false/incomplete data; possible suspension of registry rights until the declaration is regularized.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Independent certified audit is compulsory if gross annual income exceeds USD 1,000,000 or total commercial assets exceed USD 500,000; below these thresholds, an unaudited financial statement may accompany the tax return unless DGI specifically requires certified statements.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: IFRS (Normas Internacionales de Información Financiera) for mandatory‑audit entities; Panamanian GAAP/PCGA simplification permitted for small taxpayers; tax basis adjustments under the Panamanian Fiscal Code.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: All Panama S.A. entities must file a beneficial ownership statement with the DGI within 30 days of incorporation and annually within 30 days after the company's anniversary date. Any transfer of registered or bearer shares triggers an immediate updated filing. Bearer shares, if used, must be held by an authorized custodian and disclosed through the custodian statement.

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 25% (flat general CIT rate on Panamanian-source net taxable income for Sociedades Anónimas).
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: 0% effective ISR on qualifying foreign-source e-commerce revenue (territorial scope) where the sale is perfected abroad and goods do not enter Panama; 8% SME reduced rate for SAs with annual gross income up to USD 200,000 (net taxable base); SEM/CEFATI export-zone exemptions phased down from 75% in 2025 to 50% in 2026, 25% in 2027 and 0% from 2028 per Law 254/2023.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Formulario 202 (Declaración Anual de Renta) filed through the DGI E-Tax 2.0 electronic portal (https://etax.dgi.gob.pa); related informative return Form 391 for transfer pricing profiles.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual, with four (4) estimated quarterly prepayments (Formulario 338 – Declaración Estimada) due in March, June, September and December.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Within three (3) months after the fiscal year-end; for a calendar-year S.A., the filing deadline is March 31 of the immediately following year. No statutory extension; late settlement accrues the Tax-Correction Index (TCI) at annual delay interest plus a 2% annual surcharge.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Total gross revenues from all commercial operations, including online retail sales of jewelry, watches and fashion accessories at contractual invoice values.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Declare all worldwide gross receipts in Line 1; foreign-source revenue (deliveries made outside Panama) is excluded from taxation via the territorial deduction in Line 16. Retain bills of lading, courier tracking, payment gateway settlement records and customer-country evidence.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Income outside the Panamanian territorial tax scope – notably foreign-source sales earned by the e-commerce operator through platforms (Stripe/PayPal) with dispatch from origin warehouses outside Panama.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident S.A. must document the place-of-performance and the absence of a Panamanian fixed establishment; purely digital sales where the vendor lacks Panamanian nexus qualify for full exclusion.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Cost of goods sold (jewelry inventory, acquisition, packaging), logistics and shipping, payment processing fees, platform commissions, advertising and administrative expenses.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Allocate costs proportionally to Panamanian-source revenue; related-party purchase invoices require transfer pricing documentation and an arm's length justification (see Form 391).

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Taxable profit computed as Line 1 minus Lines 16, 19/20 and other allowed deductions.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: For a wholly offshore e-commerce model, net taxable income should be nil or negative after excluding foreign-source revenue; any Panamanian-source segment (local deliveries, local shows) must be isolated and taxed here.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Corporate income tax computed at 25% on net taxable income from Panamanian source (or at the 8% SME rate when eligible).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Apply the statutory rate strictly on the local-source portion; do not apply treaty credits or foreign tax credits here – Panama's territorial system does not double-tax foreign income.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Credit for the four Formulario 338 estimated tax installments paid during the fiscal year.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident S.A. with no prior-year taxable income may compute installments at zero; thereafter estimates follow the previous year's tax or 20% of the annual tax projected.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Tax withheld by third parties on local interest, dividends or other Panamanian-source payments to the company.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Include Panamanian-source interest/dividends only; foreign-source withholding taxes are not creditable under the territorial system.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Determination of final tax payable after prepayments and credits, or the amount to be refunded/taken as next-year credit.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Pay the balance electronically through E-Tax 2.0. The return must be signed electronically by the taxpayer or by the licensed Panamanian attorney/registered agent holding a DGI digital stamp.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing surcharge of 10% of the tax due (minimum USD 500) plus automatic monthly delay interest at the TCI–floating rate (effective annual ~10%); omission of Form 391 triggers USD 100 per day up to USD 10,000; false declarations activate criminal tax evasion charges with imprisonment of 2–10 years and fines of 2× the tax evaded.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 10% statutory dividend withholding tax on distributions made by Panamanian SAs; reduced to 5% when the profits distributed were subject to the general corporate income tax of 25% (no preferential regime). An additional complementary dividend tax of up to 5% applies to distributions out of exempt or preferentially taxed profits to bring the combined corporate-plus-dividend burden to a 25% effective total.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: Invoke a DTA by submitting to the DGI: (1) Form 117 (Solicitud de Aplicación de Disposiciones de un CDI), (2) a certificate of tax residence (TRC) issued by the foreign beneficiary's competent authority within the same calendar year, and (3) supporting evidence of beneficial ownership under the limitations-on-benefits / principal-purpose test (MLI standards). The reduced rate may be applied at source upon DGI prior authorization, or the over-withheld amount may be reclaimed within three years via the DGI refund procedure. Panama applies the OECD Multilateral Instrument (BEPS), so DTA relief is denied to conduit structures.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Statutory withholding: 12.5% on royalties for intellectual property/license payments and 12.5% on interest paid to non-resident lenders on Panamanian-source obligations. Treaty-reduced rates generally range 5–10% for both interest and royalties depending on the treaty partner (e.g., Panama–UK, Panama–Netherlands and Panama–UAE treaties provide reduced rates subject to anti-abuse clauses).

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: USD 3,000,000 (Panamanian Balboa is pegged 1:1 to USD) in annual gross income of the taxpayer in the prior fiscal year, triggering mandatory transfer pricing Local File/documentation and filing of Form 391; a multinational group with consolidated annual gross revenue of USD 50,000,000+ must also prepare a Master File; sole transactions with related parties above USD 250,000 are the relevant operations threshold for documentation review.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Panama's Economic Substance Regulations (Law 53 of 2017 as amended by Law 70 of 2019) require SAs engaged in 'relevant activities' – including headquarters, distribution, warehousing, service centers and IP exploitation – to demonstrate local economic substance: physical premises in Panama, adequate local payroll proportionate to the activity, local management presence and quarterly substance records submitted through the DGI e-portal. An e-commerce distribution hub established in Panama with foreign sellers is in scope unless the foreign-source sales activity is performed entirely abroad with no Panamanian fixed establishment.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Intentionally misclassifying Panamanian-source sales as foreign-source revenue, understating sales made to Panamanian customers, omitting e-commerce receipts from Stripe/PayPal that flow to the S.A., or falsifying books to reduce taxable income.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Fine equal to 200% of the omitted tax plus default interest; criminal penalties under the Fiscal Code (as amended by Law 254/2023): imprisonment of 2–5 years for evasion below USD 300,000, escalated to 5–10 years where the tax omitted exceeds USD 300,000; the evasion offence applies to both the legal entity and the responsible natural persons.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Corporate veil may be pierced under Civil Code Article 2079 where fraud or abuse of legal personality is demonstrated; directors signatories of false returns are personally liable for restitution of the evaded tax, subject to asset embargoes, travel bans and imprisonment of 2–10 years.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Shell Company / Absence of Economic Substance
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Maintaining a Panamanian S.A. with no physical office, no local bank account, no Panamanian employees, no registered agent activity and no economic substance records, used solely as a pass-through vehicle for jewelry/watches e-commerce profits or protective ownership against enforcement.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Under Law 52/2017, Law 70/2019 and applicable DGI economic-presence rules: cancellation of the corporate registration in the Public Registry, fines up to USD 1,000,000, suspension of the resident agent's operating license, and denial of treaty benefits on distributions; for AML-linked shell misuse, additional sanctions of USD 10,000–1,000,000 per infraction.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and the registered agent face personal administrative sanctions, disqualification from creating new Panamanian entities for up to 10 years, and joint civil liability for all tax deficiencies of the shell; exit bans and asset freezing are available when the shell engages in money-laundering or tax-evasion structuring.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Operating e-commerce payments through Stripe/PayPal without implementing a risk-based AML program, failing to identify the ultimate beneficial owner of the S.A., structuring luxury-product sales (watches/jewelry) above USD 500 in a single cash-equivalent transaction without record-keeping, or ignoring UAF (Financial Analysis Unit) Suspicious Transaction Reports for cross-border transactions that involve high-risk jurisdictions.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Under Law 23/2015 and Decree 37/2016: corporate fines of USD 10,000 to 1,000,000 per violation or double the value of the asset/benefit, whichever is greater; serious infringements trigger criminal prosecution of the company and executives with imprisonment of 3–5 years plus judicial travel bans; the UAF may also order disgorgement of illicitly sourced profits.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors, compliance officers and the registered agent bear personal responsibility for failing to maintain KYC/AML files on payment partners and beneficial owners; they are jointly liable for corporate AML fines, may be imprisoned for 3–5 years, and may be subject to Interpol red notices and local exit bans in the event of fraudulent gateways.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Purchasing jewelry/watch inventory from a related foreign supplier (e.g., a Hong Kong group affiliate) at prices deviating from arm's length, failing to file Form 391, or refusing to provide the DGI with the Local File when the S.A. triggers the USD 3,000,000 gross revenue threshold.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: 40% surcharge on the transfer pricing adjustment amount plus default interest; non-filing of Form 391: USD 100 per day up to USD 10,000; submission of inaccurate or incomplete TP documentation: USD 5,000 penalty per violation; DGI may reallocate the taxable base and recapture Panamanian tax accordingly.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who knowingly certify false TP documentation become jointly liable for the additional corporate tax and penalties; personal liability also arises when DGI demonstrates intentional profit-shifting through fictitious related-party structures, opening the door to civil restitution, travel bans and criminal charges of tax evasion.
